text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 2.7% today as oil prices surged, with U.S. crude rising to $103.37 per barrel and global crude hitting $123.10—a widening gap that benefits refiners who buy cheaper domestic oil and sell refined products into world markets. The stock also benefited from reports that mediators are pursuing U.S.-Iran negotiations, which could ease geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and reduce the risk premium baked into oil prices; tanker operators are currently running Iranian blockade routes despite escalating attacks, a sign the market sees supply disruptions as manageable for now.

The rally extends a two-week gain of 5% and reflects a broader shift: despite Trump's campaign promises to lower fuel costs, refining margins have actually expanded as fuel supplies tightened, driving profits for major oil companies higher than expected. This contradicts the political pressure on Big Oil, and the market appears to be pricing in continued strength in refining operations regardless of the rhetorical headwinds.
